description: We're a team of curious and creative students interested in space exploration, technology, and problem-solving. With experience in Python, AI, and research, we're working on ECHOES OF SPACE,​ an interactive digital museum exploring abandoned space equipment on the Moon and Mars. Our goal is to make space history engaging and accessible through creativity and technology.
summary:
Echoes of Space is an interactive 3D website that brings the stories of abandoned spacecraft on the Moon and Mars to life. Using NASA’s open data, we developed a virtual space environment where users can explore these destinations, discover spacecraft left behind, and learn about their missions through interactive models, a historical timeline, and mission information.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning the history of space exploration into an engaging experience rather than simply presenting users with lists of facts. It highlights why these spacecraft were sent, what they achieved, what scientists learned from them, and what eventually happened to them.

We believe these objects deserve more recognition because they are an important part of space exploration history. Even when a mission ends, the discoveries and contributions it leaves behind continue to matter. Every mission leaves something behind, and every object has a story worth telling.
details:
Echoes of Space is an interactive 3D website designed to make learning about abandoned spacecraft more engaging. It allows users to explore a virtual space environment featuring the Moon and Mars, rotate around each destination, and discover spacecraft left behind during past missions. A historical timeline lets users travel through different years and see how space exploration developed over time. By selecting a spacecraft, users can access information about its mission, purpose, achievements, and what eventually happened to it.

The project addresses NASA’s challenge by turning space history into an interactive experience rather than presenting information through ordinary articles or lists. It helps students and space enthusiasts understand not only what was left behind, but also why these objects matter and what scientists learned from their missions.

We aim to make space exploration more accessible, especially for younger audiences, while encouraging curiosity about science and technology. The creative aspect of our project comes from combining a 3D environment, spacecraft exploration, and a historical timeline into one experience. Instead of simply reading about a mission, users can explore its history themselves.

We developed the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for the 3D environment. We also used NASA’s open data as a foundation for the project's content. Throughout development, we considered ease of use, accessibility, scientific accuracy, and making the experience enjoyable across different devices. Our goal is to show that even spacecraft that are no longer active still have stories worth discovering.
